request_summary: Add two CI steps to the existing test-plugin-install workflow: run the new skill-catalog validator with its unit test, and a generated-distribution drift check that regenerates build-agent-dist output and fails on a non-empty git status.
rationale: C2: bounded one-way door: deploy:.github/workflows/test-plugin-install.yml, deploy:.github/workflows/test-plugin-install.yml, deploy:declared:deployment — reduced-pipeline floor for ≤3 files in one real package; pipeline reach: no pipeline seat may edit .github/workflows/test-plugin-install.yml, so a pipeline lane could never finish this change — it is routed to the root session that ran this triage (or to the operator for any edit the root session's own grants refuse) and the handling is inline; the class above still states the change's weight (1 edit-target files / 0 package(s) (root pseudo-package excluded, Q1 2026-08-21) / 1 write-scope clusters / co-change unassessed / shape=brownfield)
entry_point: GitHub Actions CI on push and pull_request (.github/workflows/test-plugin-install.yml)
done_oracle: The CI workflow runs `node scripts/validate-catalog.js` and its test suite alongside the existing validators, and gains a step that regenerates the multi-agent distribution and fails the job when `git status --porcelain` is non-empty. No existing step is removed or reordered, and the file remains valid GitHub Actions YAML.

seam_claims.note: The ubuntu job whose step list must gain the catalog validator and the drift check.
Existing eval step that must keep running; proof the step list is order-sensitive.

no_single_gate_reason: A GitHub Actions workflow YAML has no runnable local gate: correctness is decided by GitHub's own workflow parser at push time, and the steps it declares only execute on a runner. The two declared commands are the pre-existing repo gates that must not regress as a side effect of editing the file; the YAML itself is reviewed by diff and validated by GitHub on the next push.
